transcript.text:
Thanks everyone for the details. Let me work through my checks.

First, on cart capacity: 60 drinks over 3 hours is well within what my cart can handle — that's about 20 drinks per hour, which is manageable.

On other bookings: I've confirmed my Sunday, October 6th afternoon slot is still open, so there's no conflict there.

On venue utilities: Owen, thank you — that's a critical constraint. A single 15-amp outlet means I can only run one brewer and no separate electric grinder. I can make that work by using a single brewer and pre-grinding my beans, or using a manual hand grinder on-site. That keeps me compliant.

On dietary needs: Rosa, thank you — that's essential. I will only bring sealed, clearly labeled oat milk and will not offer almond or any other nut milk. That keeps the service safe and compliant.

Now, weighing the two options: Leah, I appreciate the $700 cash offer for 4 hours, and I'm recording it as a genuine alternative. But Quinn's proposal — 3 hours, 60 drinks, in exchange for 40 edited photos — is a fair trade that also gives me professional photos I can use for my own marketing. The shorter service window and lower drink count also make it easier to stay within the power and dietary constraints.

So here's my decision: I accept Quinn's trade arrangement. Final terms — 3 hours of espresso service, 60 drinks total, single brewer only with no separate electric grinder, sealed and labeled oat milk only with no nut milks, and in return I receive 40 edited digital photographs in a private gallery. No cash changes hands. Leah's $700 cash offer is noted but I'm going with the trade.
